In the two-stage template of the standard analyses it replaces a Stage-2 constant of order $p^2/r^2$ by one of order $1$, against $Θ(p/r)$ for the sharpest contraction-based bounds. Transferring the full rate costs a leakage term, which we bound by the step-weighted gradient mass $\sum_{u\le t}η_u\|G_u\|_F$ and show tight up to a factor $\sqrt{2}$; the price is an additive $O(\log^2 T)$ floor, not a slower rate. On BERT fine-tuning at rank ratio $32/768$ the feedback decay costs under $0.008$ validation $F_1$.

papers.title: Total acyclicity of Q-shaped diagrams and N-stable categories
papers.abstract: We study total acyclicity of $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective modules. We prove that an acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagram $P$ of projective $A$-modules is totally acyclic if and only if the associated module $K_q(P)$, or equivalently $C_q(P)$, is Gorenstein projective for every $q\in \Q$. We also establish Frobenius structures on the categories of acyclic and totally acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective $A$-modules and introduce the associated defect category. Using adjunctions between $\Q$-shaped diagrams and chain complexes, we compare this category with the classical projective defect category and show that their vanishing is equivalent under a mild condition on the Serre functor of $\Q$. Finally, we apply our results to $N$-complexes and extend the $N$-stable equivalence of Brightbill and Miemietz beyond the Gorenstein setting, obtaining a triangle equivalence between the homotopy category of totally $N$-acyclic complexes of projective $A$-modules and the $N$-stable category of Gorenstein projective $A$-modules.

papers.title: Note on the random triadic process II
papers.abstract: For a fixed integer $r\geqslant 3$, the random $r$-generalized triadic process starts from a minimum weakly $K_r$-saturated graph, namely the complete $(r-1)$-partite graph $K_{1^{r-2},n-r+2}$ with $r-2$ singleton parts and one part of size $n-r+2$. At each step of the process a new edge $\boldsymbol{e}$ is added with probability $p$, provided there exists a copy of $B_{r-2}$ in $K_n$ for which $\boldsymbol{e}$ is its spine and the only edge that has not yet been added to the current graph, where $B_{r-2}$ denotes a triangular book graph consisting of $r-2$ triangles sharing a single common edge known as the spine of the book. When $r=3$, this is the random triadic process. Korándi et al. proved a sharp threshold probability ${p}= \frac 12n^{ - \frac 12}$ for the propagation of the random triadic process.Tian and Yang complemented those results by considering the final size of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when ${p}=o( n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ α(3-r)} n)$ for any fixed constant $α> \frac 12$.In this note, we further consider the sharp threshold probability $\tilde{p}_r$ for the propagation of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when $r\geqslant 4$. We prove that $\frac 12 n^{- \frac 12}<\tilde{p}_r\leqslant c\, n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ \frac 12} n$ for some positive constant $c$, and conjecture that $\tilde{p}_r= c_r\, n^{ - \frac 12}$, where $c_r= \frac 12(r-2)!^{ \frac{1}{2r-4}}\bigl( \frac{2r-5}{r-2}\bigr)^{ \frac{2r-5}{2r-4}}$.

papers.title: An explicit domain-preserving projected Milstein scheme with strong order one for stochastic systems
papers.abstract: A variety of domain-preserving numerical schemes have been developed for scalar stochastic differential equations and for several classes of multidimensional systems, including those defined on hyperrectangles and positive orthants. To accommodate more general domain constraints, we consider stochastic systems on bounded or unbounded open convex polyhedral domains, where coefficients may exhibit boundary singularities and polynomial growth. Under local regularity, growth and boundary assumptions, we establish well-posedness and integrability estimates for the exact solution. Then we construct an explicit projected Milstein scheme that preserves the domain by applying a Euclidean projection onto a step-size-dependent interior set after each Milstein update. For systems driven by multidimensional commutative noise, we prove strong order-one convergence for the maximum grid error in Lp, for suitable p > 1 and sufficiently small step sizes under additional weighted regularity and stability conditions. The proof combines these integrability estimates with local Milstein consistency, localization and weighted stability, without requiring a priori step-size-uniform moment or boundary inverse-moment bounds for the numerical approximation. Applications to constrained stochastic models and numerical experiments illustrate the observed first-order convergence behavior.

papers.title: Blow-up suppression for the Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system by Taylor--Couette flow outside a disk
papers.abstract: Taylor--Couette devices have been investigated for enzymatic reactions and cell culture, where cylinder rotation provides a means of controlling mixing and mass transfer (Schrimpf et al., AIChE J., 2021). Motivated by these applications, this paper studies blow-up suppression in the two-dimensional Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system outside the unit disk. We prove that sufficiently strong Taylor--Couette flow yields a unique global strong solution whose density and concentration are uniformly bounded in time, without smallness assumptions on the initial cell mass or the fixed initial velocity perturbation. The main difficulty is that the angular shear tends to zero at infinity, so decay estimates on bounded regions do not directly control the full solution. To overcome this difficulty, radially weighted energy estimates exploit the radial velocity to control the density and vorticity at large radii. Combining these bounds with linear decay estimates and an energy comparison with the radial chemotaxis solution yields convergence of the density in $L^2$ to the radial solution with angularly averaged initial density, uniformly on fixed finite time intervals away from $t=0$ as the rotation amplitude tends to infinity. The decay of the radial solution then makes the full density small in $L^2$ at a finite time. An energy estimate preserves this smallness and gives global continuation.

papers.title: A decoupled structure-preserving scheme for pressure-driven multispecies tumor growth
papers.abstract: We propose an Onsager-based scheme for an $m$-species pressure-driven reaction--cross-diffusion system with a common homeostatic pressure. The scheme uses a modified scalar energy structure to update the total density, followed by compatible updates of the individual species. The global nonlinear problem remains scalar, and the species densities sum exactly to the updated total density. We establish unique solvability and show that the scheme preserves species nonnegativity, the pressure bound and total-mass monotonicity and satisfies a discrete energy dissipation law without a time-step restriction. We further develop a predictor--corrector extension to improve temporal accuracy while retaining these structural properties. Numerical experiments verify the accuracy and structure-preserving properties of the proposed schemes and demonstrate their computational efficiency.

papers.title: A Uniform Positive Lower Bound for the Analyticity Radius of KdV on the Real Line
papers.abstract: We show that, for the Korteweg--de Vries equation on the real line with real-valued initial data in an $L^2$-based analytic class, the radius of spatial analyticity of the solution has a fixed positive lower bound for all time. This improves the previous quantitative lower bounds, which tend to zero as $|t|\to\infty$. The proof uses a positive measure representation of the Hamiltonian multipliers to sum the KdV Hamiltonians into an exactly conserved energy that controls the analytic norm.

papers.title: Covering Location Optimization at GPU Speed
papers.abstract: Large-scale covering location optimization often involves NP-hard combinatorial problems that pose substantial computational challenges in urban facility planning. This paper proposes a GPU-accelerated parallel search framework for the maximal covering location problem, combining device-resident multi-trajectory exploration with lightweight CPU-side coordination. Exploiting the structure of one-swap moves, exact incremental gains are evaluated through sparse coverage representations and tiled CUDA kernels. A hierarchical reduction identifies the best exchange without materializing the full swap-gain matrix, while GPU-resident destroy-and-repair and elite-guided restarts balance intensification and diversification. Computational experiments on nine real-world urban configurations demonstrate consistent improvements over GRASP, achieving a mean relative gap of 0.029\% against published best-known solutions (BKS) and reaching BKS in 50 of 90 independent runs. On the largest urban benchmark, Kings, with 7,730 candidate locations and a budget of 50 facilities, the proposed method reaches BKS in all ten runs using a consumer-grade NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti GPU, requiring only 45.2 seconds on average to obtain its final incumbent, compared with 99.5 seconds reported for AILS-PR in a high-performance computing cluster environment. The source code and benchmark reproduction scripts are publicly available at https://github.com/Yuntian-Zhang/GPU4CO

papers.title: Interference Bounds and Merge-Aware Training Dynamics for Composable Fine-Tuned Models
papers.abstract: Combining fine-tuned models by composing their parameter updates has become a standard alternative to multi-task training. We formalize composability as a property of a collection of task vectors and prove that the excess loss of the merged model is controlled by an interference functional of the cross-task curvature overlap and the signed alignment of the updates. In the quadratic regime this functional equals the excess loss, giving a criterion that is necessary as well as sufficient and that measures the angle between task vectors in the curvature metric rather than the Euclidean one. Fine-tuning under a curvature-guided regularizer -- constructed from curvature statistics of the kind memory-efficient optimizers maintain -- keeps displacement in the base curvature metric below a ceiling set by the penalty coefficient at every iterate, at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ non-convex rate. Under a single Loewner comparison between the base statistic and the task curvatures, this control converts into a ceiling on the interference functional, inversely proportional to the penalty coefficient, so that the curvature term of the bound is controlled during training. A first-order term, present because regularized solutions are not stationary for the task loss, is not reduced in the same way. Experiments on an exact non-quadratic model confirm the budget and the ceiling, show the first-order term dominating for strong penalties, and find the curvature-guided penalty slightly better than an isotropic one. In a three-seed transformer study the functional is rank-correlated with merging degradation, but no more strongly than the Euclidean displacement norm.

papers.title: Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; if the $d$-fold cyclic cover of $X$ along the map is formal, the same holds at every $d$-th root of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other. We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime $p$. Each condition amounts to the vanishing of certain Massey products along the class of the map; together they say that the rational cochains of every finite cyclic cover along the map, and the mod-$p$ cochains of $X$, are formal as DG modules over the cohomology of the circle. For the complement of a central hyperplane arrangement, with its Milnor fibration, Alexander formality holds exactly when the numbers of hyperplanes in its irreducible factors have no common divisor greater than 1; so the complement of an irreducible arrangement of two or more hyperplanes is never Alexander formal, although it is formal. On the side of covers, we show that a CDGA graded by an abelian group, over a field of characteristic zero in which the characters of the group separate its points, is formal if and only if it is formal as a graded CDGA. Consequently, the strong formality of Kohno and Pajitnov implies formality of every finite abelian cover of $X$; the converse fails, through a Jordan block at an eigenvalue of infinite order, which no finite cover detects. Modulo $p$, eigenvalues of $p$-power order collide with 1, producing Jordan blocks that strong formality allows. The two conditions are incomparable; all four resulting classes contain arrangement complements.

papers.title: Rational Elliptic Period Relations Across Realizations: Complex Lattices, Local p-adic Periods, and Drinfeld Modules
papers.abstract: We determine the algebraic relations among full de Rham comparison periods of elliptic curves over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_p$. The connected local monodromy group gives the transcendence degree and an explicit affine linear relation ideal for the full matrix in Fontaine's field $B_{\mathrm{dR}}$. After normalizing the holomorphic row and reducing to $\mathbb C_p$, the transcendence degree drops by one and the normalized determinant supplies the additional relation. Every polynomial relation of degree at most $d$ is detected modulo $t^{d+1}$. For $d\ge1$ this bound is sharp for each elliptic curve. A rational quasi-period row gives a Galois-stable Tate line. Together with an algebraic holomorphic period ratio it forces potential splitting, which identifies the exact ordinary CM obstruction. We compute the full Tate matrix. For ordinary non-CM curves with $p\ge5$, the standard quasi-period row is rational precisely at a zero of Katz's $E_{2,p}$. Away from the zeros the two full ratios are algebraically independent. At the zeros, a nonzero quasi-period and the normalized holomorphic ratio have algebraically independent images in $\mathbb C_p$. The complex question that motivates these results, the analogue for Drinfeld modules, and a conditional arithmetic consequence for Katz values complete the comparison.

papers.title: Counterfactual attribution of surface-code failures under non-Pauli noise: dependence on trajectory pairing
papers.abstract: Under Pauli noise in a stabilizer memory, attributing a quantum error-correction failure to the noise that caused it has a canonical answer; under non-Pauli noise the attribution depends on how trajectories are paired with their counterfactuals. We define a failing shot's cause set, the sites whose removal alone removes the failure, and separate it from pairing-independent net effects. The pairing enters wherever a fixed random draw meets a Born probability; making it maximal at every random step selects shared random numbers, while continuity does not. In a distance-three surface code, exact non-Pauli noise and its Pauli twirl fail at rates equivalent within a registered margin, yet under shared draws 20.2% of exact-noise failures need three or more sites, against 2.3% under the twirl. Other admissible pairings move the mean coherent cause count from 1.61 to 80 times the minimum the marginals allow, yet pairing-independent quantities barely separate the two models. Shot-level attributions should therefore state their pairing and report pairing-independent effects alongside.

papers.title: Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, II. Operator-Theoretic Tools
papers.abstract: This is the second part of a two-part work on semiclassical Weyl laws and Connes' integration formulas for spectral triples. It establishes three operator-theoretic results, which are used in Part I but are of independent interest. The first is a factorization formula for the fractional commutators $[|D|^{-α},a]$, which is obtained by means of double operator integrals. The second is an enhancement, for arbitrary unital spectral triples, of a lemma of Connes-Sukochev-Zanin on the differences $(a^{1/2}|D|^{-α}a^{1/2})^s-|D|^{-αs}a^s$, together with a holomorphic version of it. The third is a Tauberian theorem showing that zeta function and heat trace conditions of the type sought by Connes imply Weyl laws for the operators $aD^2a$, where $a$ ranges over positive invertible elements of the algebra. Along the way, we obtain a version for spectral triples of the Tauberian theorem of McDonald-Sukochev-Zanin without any extra regularity assumption or restriction on the degree of summability. This paper can be read largely independently of Part I.

papers.title: Affine Boosted Gauss Curvature Flow
papers.abstract: We prove convexity in the affine orbit of entropies associated to Gauss curvature flow for sub-affine powers. This allows the construction of an affine boosted Gauss curvature flow, which keeps the evolving hypersurface at the affine minimizer of the Gaussian entropy. The modified flow has bounded isoperimetric ratio, and after rescaling it converges along a sequence of times to self-similar solutions of the Gauss curvature flow. The construction also proves existence of new self-similar solutions to Gauss curvature flow in the sub-affine regime.

papers.title: A GPU Interior-Point Solver with Macro-Element Condensation for Equilibrium-Based Plasticity
papers.abstract: Equilibrium-based conic formulations of elastoplasticity and limit analysis provide statically admissible stress fields but generate large Newton systems whose sparse factorization limits three-dimensional computations. This work develops and analyzes a macro-element condensation tailored to the Newton systems arising from primal--dual interior-point methods. Exploiting four-tetrahedron macro-elements, the method eliminates stress directions and macro-internal traction-continuity multipliers, yielding reduced systems that can be solved using positive-definite factorizations, with estimated reductions of approximately \(4\times\) in dimension and structural nonzeros relative to stress-only elimination. The validity of this elimination is established through global and macro-local nonsingularity conditions. Local nonsingularity is independent of the yield criterion in elastoplasticity, whereas in limit analysis it holds directly for Rankine and is ensured for von Mises through trace-bound augmentation. Numerical results show that, relative to stress-only elimination, the proposed condensation achieves CPU speedups of up to approximately \(2\times\) and reduces peak linear-solver memory by up to \(66.5\%\). We further develop a CUDA Fortran implementation that exploits uniform macro-local blocks through batched routines and uses cuDSS for the reduced sparse solve. This implementation achieves speedups of up to \(13.5\times\) over its CPU counterpart and up to \(87.5\times\) over MOSEK, while successfully solving the largest tested 3D problems that exceed the device-memory capacity of the GPU solver CuClarabel. For elastoplasticity, we also propose a preconditioned conjugate-gradient solver that reduces device-memory requirements relative to the direct GPU solver, at the expense of increased solution time.

papers.title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
papers.abstract: Computational homogenization requires repeated solutions of representative volume element (RVE) problems to determine the effective response transferred to the macroscale, including the homogenized stress. Here, we develop a basis-encoded, energy-based variational quantum formulation for linear-elastic computational homogenization. The reduced finite-element energy of the RVE is expressed as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem and mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian, whose ground state represents the equilibrium fluctuation field on the encoding grid. Using the Hellmann--Feynman theorem, differentiation of the strain-dependent Hamiltonian with respect to the prescribed macroscopic strain yields stress observables whose expectation values recover the conventional volume-averaged homogenized stress. A key structural result is that, although the equilibrium Hamiltonian is two-local, the stress observables are one-local. In linear elasticity, the two-qubit coupling coefficients are independent of macroscopic strain, hence, differentiation eliminates all two-qubit coupling terms, leaving only identity and single-qubit Pauli-$Z$ operators. These observables are diagonal in the same computational basis as the Ising Hamiltonian and can therefore be evaluated from the same computational-basis measurements used for the energy. Consequently, the homogenized stress can be obtained directly from the optimized quantum state using the same computational basis measurements as the Ising Hamiltonian, without requiring reconstruction of the microscopic displacement field or an additional measurement basis. Ground states are approximated using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), and the formulation is demonstrated on a two-dimensional periodic RVE.

papers.title: Strong chromatic index of graphs with Ore-degree at most nine
papers.abstract: The strong chromatic index $χ_s^{\prime}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of colors in an edgecoloring in which distinct edges at distance at most two in the line graph receive different colors. Let $θ(G)=\max _{x y \in E(G)}\left(d_G(x)+d_G(y)\right)$ denote the maximum edge weight, also called the Ore-degree, of $G$. We prove that every finite loopless multigraph $G$ with $θ(G) \leq 9$ satisfies $χ_s^{\prime}(G) \leq 28$. For simple graphs, this improves the direct greedy bound from 32 to 28. In particular, it verifies the Erdős-Nešetřil conjecture for simple graphs of maximum degree five whose vertices of degree five form an independent set, using one fewer color than the conjectured bound of 29. When $θ(G)=9$, our bound is four colors above the bound of 24 predicted by the Ore-degree conjecture of Chen, Huang, Yu, and Zhou.

papers.title: Stability analysis and critical thresholds in a nonlocal advection diffusion model of wound healing on bounded domains
papers.abstract: Nonlocal advection diffusion models describe how wound healing depends on the strength of cell-cell adhesion and the cell sensing radius. Depending on these parameters, the wound may close completely or remain in a persistent state with a spatially nonuniform cell density. The model combines random cell movement, cell proliferation, and cell-cell adhesion within a finite sensing radius. We first derive the dispersion relation on the whole line and use it to compute the critical sensing radius and the corresponding wavelength. This relation shows that diffusion and cell proliferation stabilize the healed state, while cell-cell adhesion can make it unstable. On a bounded interval, the cell density is fixed at the healthy value on an exterior collar. In this setting, we establish conditions that keep the cell density within a positive bounded range, derive a sufficient condition for nonlinear exponential stability that depends on domain size, and formulate and numerically solve the associated linear spectral problem. The analysis shows how reducing the domain size can stabilize the healed state at parameter values for which the whole line model is linearly unstable. Finally, we compute critical sensing radii and domain sizes numerically and compare the sufficient stability bounds with the transitions observed in wound simulations involving perturbations of finite amplitude.

papers.title: The Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology: A Methodological Shift from the Perspective of Natural Science and Engineering Practice
papers.abstract: Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, fundamentally driven by the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm, rely on setting external objectives and iterative trial-and-error. When confronted with complex nonlinear problems containing noise and conflicting constraints, this paradigm inherently induces statistical smoothing and compromise, yielding black-box models that lack interpretability and out-of-distribution generalization. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology, reconstructing the solving process into four irreversible stages: Deconstruction, Structure, Construction, and Solving. The method suspends a priori presuppositions to strip unit coupling, extracts rigid invariants inherent to the problem, constructs equivalent mappings anchored to these invariants, and executes the mapping directly to generate the solution. Evaluation metrics and experience are relegated to a posteriori verification. Demonstrated through cross-disciplinary practices including number theory, Hamiltonian systems, deep learning, and seismic inversion, this methodology transcends the statistical fitting bottleneck. Structure-Driven and Objective-Driven methodologies are complementary: when structure is sufficient, solutions are directly constructed; when lacking, it degenerates into the OD path.

papers.title: A proof of Casselman's comparison conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Casselman's comparison conjecture for parabolic subgroups of real linear reductive groups. Let $Q=LU$ be a standard parabolic subgroup of a real linear reductive group $G$, with Levi subgroup $L$ and unipotent radical $U$. For every Casselman--Wallach representation $π$ of $G$ and every $i\geq0$, the natural inclusion $π_K\hookrightarrowπ$ induces a topological $L$-equivariant isomorphism \[ H_i(\mathfrak u,π_K)^\infty\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H_i(\mathfrak u,π). \] Put $\mathscr U=\mathcal U(\mathfrak u)$ and $F_k=\mathscr U/I_{\mathfrak u}^k$, where $I_{\mathfrak u}$ is the augmentation ideal. For every $k\geq1$ and $i\geq0$, we establish natural topological $L$-isomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty \simeq \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π),\ \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty \simeq \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π). \end{aligned} \] We also obtain closedness of $\mathfrak u^kM$ for the (co)chain spaces $M=C_j(\mathfrak u,π),C^j(\mathfrak u,π)$, and for $M=J_a,J_{a-1}/J_a$, where $(J_a)$ is the smooth Bruhat filtration of a principal series representation.

papers.title: Dynamical edge universality and the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
papers.abstract: We prove dynamical edge universality for three families of interacting particle systems for every $β>0$: $β$-Dyson Brownian motion with an analytic potential, weighted $β$-corners processes, and a class of discrete-time Markov chains. Our results apply to general non-equilibrium initial data and show that the Airy$_β$ line ensemble emerges at positive times whenever the limiting density has a regular square-root edge. More precisely, after centering at the moving deterministic edge and rescaling space and time on the $n^{-2/3}$ and $n^{-1/3}$ scales, respectively, the trajectories of the top $k$ particles converge jointly in distribution to the top $k$ curves of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble, for every fixed $k$, in the topology of uniform convergence on compact time intervals. The proof combines dynamical loop equations with characteristic-flow estimates to establish local laws near the moving edge and upper bounds on the extremal particle. We then identify the stochastic evolution of every subsequential limit of the rescaled Stieltjes transform and establish convergence through the pole-evolution characterization of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble.

papers.title: Rigidity and Non-Rigidity of Disk Pseudo-Rotations below $C^2$
papers.abstract: For every $0<β\le1$, we prove $C^0$-rigidity of area-preserving $C^{1,β}$ disk pseudo-rotations with non-Brjuno rotation number. At the $C^1$ endpoint, every non-Brjuno rotation number of zero exponential type admits non-rigid examples. We also obtain a different rigidity result when the rotation number has positive exponential type: the boundary restriction of every $C^1$ pseudo-rotation is rigid and topologically conjugate to a rotation. We show that this boundary conclusion fails in the bi-Lipschitz class by constructing non-rigid examples for every rotation number of finite positive exponential type. The proof of rigidity is based on a finite-information closing theorem under Hölder regularity. For the construction of counterexamples, we use disjoint supports instead of a summable perturbation scheme.

papers.title: Certified pandigital approximations of $π$, $γ$, $δ$ and $e$
papers.abstract: In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $π$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $γ$ and Feigenbaum's constant $δ$ that use each of the digits $1,\dots,n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $π$, $γ$ and $δ$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the published records; for $π$ with the digits 1-9 the optimal error is $2.81\cdot 10^{-14}$. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.

papers.title: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines
papers.abstract: Most practical combinatorial optimization problems involve constraints, and an Ising machine that flips one spin at a time can respect them only through energy penalties that raise barriers between feasible solutions. Here we show that a higher-order neuromorphic Ising machine can enforce constraints through programmable transitions rather than penalties. In an autoencoder-like architecture, each inner-layer neuron represents a move, a family of multi-spin transitions that maps every feasible state to another feasible state, receives the energy change of its move through connections that outer-layer neurons multiplicatively switch on or off, and updates the state through the same connections. A compiler turns constraints into this wiring with a number of auxiliary clauses that grows only polynomially for parity, cardinality, one-hot, partition and permutation constraints. Restricting the search to feasible states reduces constraint handling to move design, and we show that the fastest-annealing moves are not those that mix fastest but those that lower the deepest energy barriers, and that moves chosen from the objective lower them further than random ones. On third-order graph matching, the machine needs orders of magnitude fewer iterations than penalty-based neuromorphic machines. Configured as a sampler on a field-programmable gate array, it decodes the surface code with maximum-likelihood accuracy up to code distance 15 within 52 $μ$s per shot and, under noisy syndrome measurements, decodes in real time for millisecond measurement rounds up to distance 9 with fewer logical errors than belief-propagation decoders.

papers.title: A complete intersection theorem for sets of bounded size
papers.abstract: Let \(1\le t\le k\le n\) and \(2k<n+t\). We prove that a largest \(t\)-intersecting family of subsets of \([n]\) of size at most \(k\) is obtained by taking all such subsets that contain at least \(t+r\) points of a fixed \((t+2r)\)-element set, for some \(0\le r\le\left\lfloor\frac{n-t}{2}\right\rfloor\). This settles a conjecture of Ahlswede, Bey, Engel and Khachatrian from 2002.

papers.title: On the regularity of stationary solutions to free boundary problems
papers.abstract: In this note, we improve the regularity of Hölder continuous stationary solutions with respect to inner variations which are harmonic outside their zero set. We obtain a $\sqrt{\log}$-Lipschitz estimate for a class of solutions allowing a generalized phase variable and including the two-phase problem. In the case of the one-phase problem, we can improve to Lipschitz regularity. In particular, we show that the initial Lipschitz assumption in the class of variational solutions considered by Kriventsov and Weiss can be replaced by any positive Hölder exponent

papers.title: Curvature-Calibrated Friction and an Exact Gauge Symmetry for Quantum Hamiltonian Descent
papers.abstract: A design problem constrained by a partial differential equation can be solved coherently on a quantum computer. The objective is block-encoded rather than measured, and Quantum Hamiltonian Descent consumes it directly. We identify two obstacles in this pipeline and repair both. First, the oracle construction assumes affine generators with positive semidefinite Hermitian parts, which covariance entries violate for every off-diagonal generator. Encoding the covariance as an affine combination of positive semidefinite atoms restores both conditions at every register point, at the price of a representational floor, median 45% of the fitted family's own objective range for a fixed rank-three dictionary and 22% with a variable diagonal. Second, adding a constant to the objective leaves the measurement distribution exactly invariant, yet the mean-objective friction heuristic in current use assigns such objectives different schedules. Calibrating the friction to the landscape curvature restores the symmetry, though not the constant in $ν= c\sqrtμ$, and a bracketed sweep at matched objective-phase exposure, not end-to-end cost, places the best tested friction between 0.032 and 0.25 of critical damping on a diffusion-design benchmark, a broad plateau an order of magnitude below the classical default.

papers.title: A Nonadaptive Sparse Fourier Transform in Every Dimension
papers.abstract: Let $G=(\mathbb{Z}/2^a\mathbb{Z})^d$, of order $N=2^{ad}$. Given point-query access to any complex signal $X$ with Fourier transform $\hat{X}$ over $G$, we provide a randomized algorithm that constructs a $k$-sparse estimate $\widetilde{X}$ via non-adaptive queries such that, with large probability, $\|\widetilde{X}-\hat{X}\|_2^2 \leq C \cdot \|H_k(\hat{X})-\hat{X}\|_2^2$, for an absolute constant $C>0$, where $H_k(\cdot)$ denotes the best $k$-sparse approximation. The constant $C$ can be improved to any desired $1+\varepsilon$ by either supplying a constant-factor estimate on the $k$-sparse tail norm or allowing an arbitrarily small additive error term $δ\|\hat{X}\|_2^2$ on the right-hand side. With a supplied tail estimate, we can also satisfy an $\ell_\infty/\ell_2$ heavy hitters guarantee. For fixed $δ$, the number of samples is $O((k/\varepsilon^2)(\log N)\log(k/\varepsilon))$, and the recovery algorithm requires a polynomial in $(k/\varepsilon)\log N$ exact operations. The algorithm naturally extends to $G=(\mathbb{Z}/b^a\mathbb{Z})^d$ for any fixed integer $b>1$.

papers.title: The Semi--Fibonacci Partition Tree
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce a binary tree in which every semi-Fibonacci partition appears exactly once. The left--right address of a vertex gives an explicit formula for the parts of the corresponding partition and encodes statistics such as the largest $2$-adic valuation among its parts. We construct a sign-reversing involution that refines Andrews's parity theorem by determining the difference between the numbers of partitions of a given integer at even and odd depths. Inspired by properties of the Calkin--Wilf tree, we study several parameters of our tree and use them to obtain new results on semi-Fibonacci partitions. We also derive generating functions for partition statistics and determine the average and extremal partition sizes at each level.

papers.title: Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer. We obtain the asymptotic order of growth for both the number of group elements and the number of conjugacy classes in $G$, with length at most $L$, and fixed genus (orientable or non-orientable) $n$. For free groups, our methods give precise asymptotics for each of the counts.

papers.title: Gaussian Quasi-Likelihood Estimation for Nonsynchronously Observed Lévy processes
papers.abstract: We study parametric inference for a two-dimensional simple Lévy process observed at high frequency over an expanding time horizon, where the two components are sampled in a possibly non-synchronous manner. Combining Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimation for Lévy SDEs with the non-synchronous quasi-likelihood methodology, we construct a Gaussian-type quasi-likelihood based on the covariance structure of non-synchronous increments, and we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the resulting estimators. The convergence rates coincide with those in the synchronous setting, while the asymptotic variance depends essentially on the sampling design and becomes more complicated under non-synchronicity. To handle the different moment structure of pure-jump Lévy processes, we introduce an additional convergence assumption and provide tractable sufficient conditions linked to the observation scheme. Numerical experiments illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators.

papers.title: Generation of coherent-state Schrödinger cat states in a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model implemented with Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: We investigate the generation of coherent-state Schrödinger cat states using a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model (JCM) implemented in a Josephson-junction quantum circuit. We consider a specific superconducting flux-qubit implementation and estimate the resulting two-photon coupling constant. We numerically examine three types of noise: magnetic flux noise with $1/f$ fluctuations, energy relaxation associated with the flux-qubit $T_{1}$ decay, and photon loss in the bosonic mode obtained by quantizing the phase variable of the dc SQUID used for qubit readout. We find that photon loss has a particularly significant effect on cat-state fidelity. We also investigate the time evolution of the probability-amplitude distribution in the Pegg-Barnett phase-state basis for the $l$-photon JCM ($l=1,2,3,4$), starting from a coherent bosonic state. Finally, we assume that the bosonic mode is initially prepared in a displaced thermal state and then decoupled from the heat bath. We study the subsequent unitary evolution to determine how the initial temperature affects the fidelity and Wigner function of the generated cat states.

papers.title: Kakutani equivalence of higher rank unipotent abelian actions I
papers.abstract: We study Kakutani equivalence of higher-rank abelian unipotent actions. We construct a Kakutani invariant for general $\mathbb{R}^n$-actions and establish a quantitative vanishing criterion. By this criterion, we prove that ergodic abelian horocyclic actions on finite-volume quotients of connected semisimple Lie groups are loosely Kronecker. We also include a proof of the Abramov entropy formula for time changes of Rn-actions, following the strategy developed by Nadler.

papers.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function III
papers.abstract: We extend the denumerant to a weighted denumerant, the sum of a function $μ$ over the solutions in non-negative integers of $a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=n$. For the monomial weights $x_1^{α_1}\cdots x_k^{α_k}$, with exponents $α_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$, we prove upper and lower bounds of the kind of those of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689), with an explicit constant and explicit shifts. As an example of application, summing these bounds over all the numbers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ we find, by elementary means, the asymptotic main term of the sums $\sum_{y_1+\cdots+y_k=n}σ_{α_1}(y_1)\cdotsσ_{α_k}(y_k)$ of products of divisor functions, for every $k$ and for real exponents $α_i\neq0$ of either sign.

papers.title: Variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups
papers.abstract: We develop fixed-step variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups, derive their reduced dynamics, and analyze their long-time behavior by backward error analysis. We derive the continuous Euler-Lagrange equations, energy balance, and Noether conservation laws, and construct time-indexed discrete Lagrangians using retractions, with the midpoint-Cayley scheme treated explicitly. On their regularity domains, the resulting phase-space maps are symplectic. For left-invariant discrete Lagrangians, they reduce to Lie-Poisson maps that preserve coadjoint orbits and, when $G$ is connected, every Casimir function. A variational error analysis establishes second-order accuracy of the midpoint-Cayley method. We also construct an exactly symplectic, projectable extension on $T^*(\mathbb R\times G)$ whose formal modified Hamiltonian is affine in the momentum conjugate to time and admits symmetry reduction. Under uniform analyticity, coefficient bounds, and domain-containment assumptions, optimal truncation yields exponentially accurate interpolation and near-conservation of the modified extended Hamiltonian over exponentially long intervals. For a connected attitude network on $SO(3)^N$ with damping and uniformly positive, non-increasing coupling weights, we prove local asymptotic stability of the static consensus set for the continuous dynamics and exact preservation of total spatial momentum by the discrete scheme. Numerical experiments on the network and on a time-dependent rigid body on $SO(3)$ illustrate second-order convergence and the extended energy balance.

papers.title: Compilation-informed probabilistic logical-error cancellation
papers.abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41534-026-01407-8Compilation-informed probabilistic logical-error cancellation

papers.title: High-key-rate fully-passive quantum access network with thermal source
papers.abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41534-026-01412-xHigh-key-rate fully-passive quantum access network with thermal source

papers.title: Proof Checking Continuous Reachability
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a proof format and proof checker for certifying reachability computations of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with polynomial vector fields. Establishing a proof checking framework for certifying ODE reachability is similar to the checking of UNSAT proofs for propositional satisfiability solving, but it is even more important due to the challenges inherent in dealing with ODEs, and even more challenging due to the numerical nature of ODE reachability algorithms. The proofs are expressed in differential dynamic logic (dL), and can be independently verified with symbolic theorem provers for dL (e.g. KeYmaeraX). Such proofs are naturally generated by reachability algorithms based on Taylor models, a popular technique to obtain rigorous bounds on approximations of ODEs. This paper proves the completeness of such proofs - if an approximation was correctly computed by some (possibly untrusted) reachability algorithm via Taylor models, then a corresponding proof in dL can be automatically generated and checked to be correct in dL's proof calculus. A dedicated proof checker is implemented in Lean4 for improved performance, which is capable of formally verifying benchmarks in the ARCH competition.

papers.title: Quantum dynamical transitions when the corresponding classical phase space has a separatrix: extension of the QKNH theorem beyond double wells
papers.abstract: In classical Hamiltonian systems with a slowly time-dependent parameter, adiabaticity breaks down at a separatrix, leading to probabilistic post-adiabatic transitions between different phase-space regions described by the Kruskal-Neishtadt-Henrard (KNH) theorem. Quantum mechanically, dynamical tunneling allows adiabaticity to persist where it breaks down classically, making the quantum-classical correspondence for separatrix crossing non-trivial. We recently established a quantum version of the KNH theorem (QKNH) by introducing the concept of a sweep-rate-dependent quantum separatrix in the instantaneous energy spectrum of the time-dependent system. The QKNH theorem relates the splitting of a quantum ensemble between the outgoing dynamical sectors at the quantum separatrix to their relative growth rates, and thus provides a quantum analog of the classical KNH rule. Here, we demonstrate that these findings are not restricted to double-well systems with tunneling through a potential barrier. We investigate a slowly driven quantum pendulum, in which the avoided crossings arise from above-barrier reflection. The resulting Landau-Zener probabilities have the same local lattice form as in the double-well problem, allowing the application of the QKNH theorem.

papers.title: Kernel Regression using Persistence Diagrams
papers.abstract: Persistence diagrams are widely used in topological data analysis to summarize topological and geometric structure in data. We study nonparametric regression where inputs are persistence diagrams and outputs are real-valued. Using kernel-based local averaging estimators defined directly over diagram space with Wasserstein distance, we establish consistency and derive bounds on the rate of convergence under suitable assumptions in the $L^2$-theory. We also present computational experiments that demonstrate strong performance of the proposed estimator, particularly in low data regimes.

papers.title: Large Gaps Between Piatetski-Shapiro Primes
papers.abstract: A Piatetski-Shapiro prime is a prime number that can be written as $\lfloor m^c \rfloor$ for some positive integer $m$ and non-integer $c>1$. Li and Pan showed the results for small gaps between consecutive Piatetski-Shapiro primes for $1<c<9/8$. On the other hand, Deshouillers, Drmota, and Müllner showed the large gaps between Piatetski-Shapiro primes although they did not mention it explicitly whenever there are infinitely many Piatetski-Shapiro primes with exponent $c$ using binomial expansion. In this article, we use a different method from theirs, and we obtain the explicit exponent that appears in their paper.

papers.title: Pointwise Minmax Representations for Total Variation Denoising on Graphs
papers.abstract: Total variation denoising (TVD) is a fundamental method in image denoising, signal processing, and nonparametric regression. We establish exact pointwise minmax/maxmin representations for TVD on arbitrary finite graphs, extending recent one-dimensional results. Under squared loss, fitted values are expressed through corrected local averages over nested connected vertex sets. The correction is a signed boundary count: edges leaving the inner set contribute +1 if they remain within the outer set and -1 otherwise. To the best of our knowledge, this representation is new even for two-dimensional TVD. We show that Brunk's classical minmax formulas for isotonic regression on every finite directed acyclic graph arise as special cases of our graph TVD representation. The exact reduction proceeds through asymmetric TVD and nearly isotonic regression, which coincides with isotonic regression above a finite penalty threshold. We further extend the representations to arbitrary finite separable convex losses, assuming coercivity of the full objective, but without requiring differentiability or strict convexity. For nonunique solutions, the possible fitted values at each coordinate form a compact interval. Its lower and upper endpoints admit maxmin and minmax representations, respectively, through scalar local optimization problems and are attained simultaneously at all coordinates by two extremal solutions. This yields exact representations for quantile TVD on arbitrary graphs and unifies TVD, nearly isotonic regression, and isotonic regression within a single pointwise framework for general separable convex losses.

papers.title: Resilience of emergent Hamiltonian quantum memories in the presence of noise
papers.abstract: Emergent Hamiltonians can freeze an entangled state prepared through coherent evolution, since that state is an eigenstate of the Hamiltonian under which it is then stored. We show that the freedom left in this construction allows the storage spectrum to be adapted to a noisy environment without changing the stored state. For a product of Bell pairs prepared from a density wave in an engineered chain, a selection rule prevents local density noise from connecting the target to any of its degenerate partners, so that rescaling the storage Hamiltonian by a factor $α$ moves every transition this noise drives. Under $1/f$ noise, the storage time then grows in proportion to $α$, a result we confirm by evolving the memory under explicit classical $1/f$ fields, whereas for an Ohmic bath the most favorable scale depends on its cutoff. Fermionic loss, treated as a solvable model, includes a transition that rescaling leaves at zero frequency, and an energy shift $μ$ per particle moves it away from zero, with an exact orbital solution giving the resulting lifetimes. Finally, among number-conserving quadratic reference Hamiltonians, $α$ and $μ$ are the only controls that keep the storage Hamiltonian nearest neighbor at every time along the preparation, so that the protocol combines local freezing with control over the storage spectrum.

papers.title: Exceptional zeros for $\mathrm{GSp}(4) \times \mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Yoshida lifts
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to study an exceptional zero phenomenon for the $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\mathrm{GSp}_4\times\mathrm{GL}_2$ in the critical regions (F) and (D). We construct improved $p$-adic $L$-functions by replacing the $p$-depleted Eisenstein family with its $p$-ordinary counterpart. Under a local compatibility hypothesis at the ramified places and classical control for the families, we show that their poles detect exactly the Yoshida lifts whose smaller constituent is dual to the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ representation. The proof compares their residues with distinguished automorphic periods, extending the coherent period formula to the case where one modular form has weight zero. An explicit Euler-factor identity relates each improved function to the usual $p$-adic $L$-function. At these Yoshida points, the vanishing factor cancels the pole, and the resulting value is expressed through the distinguished period and the logarithmic derivative of the ordinary elliptic root. We also discuss the expected factorization along Yoshida families into Hida--Rankin $p$-adic $L$-functions.

papers.title: Preservation of big diagonal for automorphisms of Hilbert schemes
papers.abstract: If $X$ is a smooth projective surface that is not K3 or abelian surface, we show that any automorphism of the Hilbert scheme of points $X^{[n]}$ preserves the big diagonal. This generalizes several previous works, and gives a complete description of automorphisms of $X^{[n]}$ when $X$ is not K3 or abelian surface. We also obtain a Torelli-type theorem: a smooth projective surface $X$ can be recovered from $X^{[n]}$ unless $X$ is a K3 surface. Further, for each integer $n\geq 2$, we construct automorphisms of $A^{[n]}$ not preserving the big diagonal for an abelian surface $A$.

papers.title: Moduli of continuity preserved by the Hilbert Transform
papers.abstract: It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as Hölder continuity. In~\cite{GS01}, M. Goldstein and W. Schlag provided a criterion, based on two simple conditions, for a modulus of continuity to be preserved under the Hilbert transform. These conditions are not satisfied by the weak-Hölder and the log-Hölder moduli of continuity. More recently, A. Avila, Y. Last, M. Shamis and Q. Zhou proved in~\cite{ALSZ21} that for compactly supported $t$-log-Hölder continuous functions ($t>1$) their Hilbert transforms are at least $(t-1)$-log-Hölder continuous. A similar result holds for weak-Hölder continuous functions. In this note we extend these results to a class of continuous functions satisfying a couple of mild integrability conditions.

papers.title: DS3M: Deep structured state space models for nonlinear system identification on modern hardware
papers.abstract: Neural state-space identification learns dynamical models from measured inputs and outputs. SUBNET combines this task with an encoder that estimates initial states from short measurement histories. Its continuous-time version requires many successive neural-network evaluations during numerical integration, resulting in slow training speed which is a major limitation for practical use cases. We propose deep structured state space models (DS3M), which combine compact nonlinear dynamical components in parallel and in series. Custom GPU kernels implemented with Triton reduce the launch and memory overhead of their sequential evaluation. We explain this construction, describe a port-Hamiltonian variant, and present various benchmark comparisons of accuracy and training time.

papers.title: On the non-extendibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ with $n = 2k^2 \pm k$
papers.abstract: We study a class of Diophantine problems arising from triangular analogues of classical Diophantine tuples. A set of positive integers is called a triangular $D(n)$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by $n$, is a triangular number. In this paper, we investigate the extensibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs of the form $\{n,2n\}$, where $n = 2k^2 + \varepsilon k$, with $k$ an odd positive integer and $\varepsilon \in \{-1,1\}$ such that $4k + \varepsilon$ is prime. We prove that for all $(k,\varepsilon)$ in a finite explicitly determined set, the pair $\{n,2n\}$ cannot be extended to a triangular $D(n)$-quadruple. The obtained results give further evidence for a general non-extensibility phenomenon, which we formulate as a conjecture.

papers.title: Integer Programming Strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box Problem
papers.abstract: We present a selection of Integer Programming (IP) strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box problem, which asks for the longest induced path in the $d$-dimensional hypercube. Current records are based on sophisticated, exhaustive searches, with optimality proven only for instances up to dimension 8, motivating our study of IP formulations. We address symmetries and potential strengthenings. With the smallest open instance having as few as 512 binary decision variables, the proposed IPs offer a challenging and intriguing combinatorial problem. In addition, we extend the problem to higher-dimensional grid graphs and provide solutions for unexplored and unsolved instances.

papers.title: Algebraic independence of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms via period interpretations
papers.abstract: Based on Hartl's de Rham-crystalline comparison isomorphism, we formulate a notion of André's $v$-adic periods for a class of Anderson $\mathbb{F}_q[z]$-motives with respect to a degree-one finite place $v$ of a rational function field over a finite field, following Ancona-Frăţilă's formulation of $p$-adic periods. The formulation naturally produces deformation series of the resulting periods and Frobenius difference equations satisfied by these series. We then explain how the formulation brings the resulting $v$-adic periods within the scope of Chen's $v$-adic ABP criterion and of difference Galois theory, and gives us a strategy to study the transcendence degrees of $v$-adic periods through their deformation series. We show that certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms can be expressed in terms of André's $v$-adic periods. Applying the strategy to these examples, we obtain algebraic independence results for certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms; more precisely, the transcendence degree of the field generated by a suitable collection of special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms is one less than the transcendence degree of the field generated by the corresponding special values of $\infty$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms together with the Carlitz period.

papers.title: Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture
papers.abstract: Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture. Reducing the characteristic polynomial modulo $4$ gives a necessary condition for nilpotency that is linear over $\F$. For $m > 1$ it forces $u = (v, 1, i, \rev v)$ or $u = (v, i, 1, \rev v)$, and an identity implicit in Corless's proof then reduces the problem to $v$. Since $T_m(u)$ is diagonally similar to a finite section of the Feinberg--Zee hopping matrix, the theorem also determines the nilpotent tridiagonal sign matrices. We further show that the $(1,1)$ entry of the resolvent of a nilpotent $T_m(u)$ is $λ^{-1} \pm λ^{-3} \pm λ^{-7} \pm \dots \pm λ^{-(2^K - 1)}$, with signs that determine $u$. The proof of the main theorem has been formalised in Lean~4.

papers.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function II
papers.abstract: We apply the elementary arithmetic argument of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689) to binomial coefficients, and obtain upper and lower bounds for Sylvester's denumerant function for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ that sharpen those of Agnarsson. The lower bound is a sum of binomial coefficients; it holds along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ without assuming that a solution exists, and it is greater than the polynomial lower bound of the first paper. In the upper bound the shift of Agnarsson's binomial coefficient is reduced.

papers.title: A fast iterative solver for lopsided Sylvester matrix equations
papers.abstract: A generalization of the factored alternating direction implicit algorithm is introduced that makes use of type $(p, q)$ Zolotarev rational functions to apply unequal numbers of left and right shifts. Convergence properties of the algorithm are discussed, as well as a method for computing shift parameters. Several applications are highlighted where the generalized method is useful, including in the solving of a collection of shifted linear systems, for discretizations that involve left and right operators that are not equally amenable to inversion, and for Sylvester matrix equations with differently-sized, differently-structured, or differently-conditioned coefficient matrices.

papers.title: A note on Turán densities of daisies and hypergraph products
papers.abstract: The Turán density of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ is defined as $π(\mathcal{H})=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})/\binom{n}{r}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal H)$ denotes the largest number of edges in an $\mathcal H$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $r\geq s\geq2$ and $t\geq s$, an $(r,s,t)$-daisy $\mathcal D_r(s,t)$ is the $r$-uniform hypergraph consisting of all unions of a fixed $(r-s)$-set with the $s$-subsets of a disjoint $t$-set. We show that for every fixed $s\geq3$, \[ \lim_{r\rightarrow\infty}π(\mathcal D_r(s,t))=1-O_s(t^{-(s-1)}) \] as $t\rightarrow\infty$. This bound is best possible up to the implicit constant by a classical result of de Caen, and it answers, in a stronger form, a question of Ellis, Ivan and Leader, who asked for the case $s=3$. Moreover, we show a related result for matroid basis hypergraphs. We also consider Turán densities of hypergraph products, of which daisies are a special case. The product of two hypergraphs on disjoint vertex sets consists of all unions of an edge of the first with an edge of the second. For the product $\mathcal H^d$ of $d$ disjoint copies of a fixed $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ that is not $r$-partite, we show that $1-π(\mathcal H^d) \rightarrow 0$ exponentially fast as $d\rightarrow\infty$, and we determine the exponential rate in terms of the minimum number of edges in a homomorphic image of $\mathcal H$. This answers a question of Bollobás, Leader and Malvenuto up to a polynomial factor in $d$, and we further address a related question of theirs for products of two different hypergraphs.

papers.title: Interior and global $W^{2,1}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that for $3\leq k\leq n-1$, continuous $k$-convex solutions of the $k$-Hessian equation with density bounded above and below by positive constants belong to $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$. This regularity holds globally on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex domains when both the boundary and the boundary values are of class $C^{1,1}$.

papers.title: The upper copula capacity
papers.abstract: Many problems in statistics, combinatorics, econometrics, and other fields are expressible in terms of the upper probability of all copulas. We formally study this capacity, which we call the upper copula capacity, as a mathematical object. In particular, we examine the capacity of given sets and integration with respect to this capacity. For two-dimensional convex sets, the upper copula capacity equals the smaller of the two coordinate projection lengths. We also give an exact formula for the capacity of lower-tail events for positively weighted sums in any dimension and characterize when the upper Choquet integral equals the supremum of expectations over all copulas. Various problems in different fields can be formulated via the upper-copula capacity, and we discuss how known and new results connect to offer new perspectives on these problems.

papers.title: The 1d Stochastic Dirac Operator
papers.abstract: We introduce a random Dirac operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R}^2)$ that we call $1d$ Stochastic Dirac Operator and which is indexed by two parameters $κ_0,κ$. In two companion articles, we show that this operator arises generically as the small disorder limit of one-dimensional random Schrödinger operators, thus revealing a universal behavior. In the present paper, we provide a detailed construction of this singular operator, and investigate its spectral properties. In particular, we show that its spectrum is either absolutely continuous when $κ= 0$, or pure point when $κ>0$. In the latter case, we show that the shape of the eigenfunctions is given by the exponential of a two sided Brownian motion with drift, in connection with a result of Rifkind and Virág. Finally, we establish a delicate convergence result of the sequence of eigenvalues / eigenfunctions from the finite-volume operator to the infinite-volume one.

papers.title: Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons
papers.abstract: We prove that complete expanding Kähler-Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in Stein manifolds, and hence pseudoconvexity of bounded domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete Kähler-Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces. If $D$ is a relatively compact Stein domain in a reduced pure-dimensional Stein space of dimension at least two and $\operatorname{Sing} D$ is finite and nonempty, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Reg} D)$ is compact, excluding nontrivial expanders with complete soliton fields.

papers.title: The Bolker condition and overdetermined FBI transforms
papers.abstract: We study real analytic canonical relations satisfying the Bolker condition and show that, in the FBI representation, they can be described by phases of overdetermined FBI transforms. As an application, we give a simplified proof of an analytic regularity result for generalized Radon transforms due to Mazzucchelli-Salo-Tzou.

papers.title: Certified Separation Between Coherent and Adaptive Temporal Processing of Quantum-Error-Correction Readout
papers.abstract: Repeated quantum-error-correction readout is normally converted into a classical time series: each syndrome pulse is measured on arrival and only the resulting classical record is retained. Nonorthogonal readout signals raise the question of whether preserving quantum information between rounds can improve the final recovery decision. We formulate this comparison as a loss-weighted state-discrimination problem. For an idealized two-round benchmark with quadrature phase-shift-keying (QPSK) signals, a receiver with a seven-dimensional persistent register has certified recovery-decision error below $24.2100\%$, whereas every separate adaptive receiver has error above $25.1431\%$. The certified separation is at least $0.933$ percentage points. The loss counts incorrect final error-mask decisions in the benchmark. In the strict architecture, where the counted register is the entire persistent state, four dimensions are necessary and sufficient to outperform the adaptive class. Certified separations also occur at three and four rounds with register dimensions $8$ and $36$, compared with $16$ and $64$ for full-prefix storage. We relate memory dimension to the structure of the temporal measurement, give a sufficient memory bound for collective measurements, and quantify robustness to register dephasing and accumulated channel error.

papers.title: The geometry and classification of positive frames
papers.abstract: We investigate the geometric and operator-theoretic structure of positive frames and their duals in finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, with particular emphasis on positive linear dependence, redundancy, and convex geometry. Building on the classical theory of positive spanning sets, we characterize equivalence classes of positive frames through the kernels of their synthesis operators and obtain parametrizations in terms of the relative interior of a standard simplex and suitable subsets of Grassmannians. We establish that every redundant frame admits a positive dual, regardless of whether the original frame is positive, and provide an explicit construction through a rank-one perturbation of the canonical dual. Furthermore, we investigate the affine and topological structure of positive dual frames, proving their relative openness in the space of all duals and the absence of extreme points. We characterize dual frames satisfying prescribed positive relations and derive criteria for the existence of positive-basis duals. We also examine semi-positive frames and their boundary behavior, together with connections between positive spanning, balancedness, and finite group representations. Finally, we study the convex geometry of nonnegative relation spaces and establish a directional characterization of positive-spanning robustness under arbitrary vector erasures. These results provide a unified geometric framework for understanding positive frames, their dual systems, and the role of redundancy in constrained reconstruction.

papers.title: Extinction conditions for a two-sex branching process with random mating and overlapping generations
papers.abstract: We propose a modification of the bisexual branching process with random mating and overlapping generations. Unlike the model of Molina and Mota \cite{Molina2024}, our modification introduces probabilistic age-dependent survival that depends on the state of the population. Our modification preserves the general properties of the original process. We establish two sufficient conditions characterizing the subcritical and supercritical regimes of the process, i.e., extinction of the population with probability one and survival of the population with positive probability.The results are illustrated with numerical simulations of the process performed in Python.

papers.title: On generalizations of the Cohen structure theorem
papers.abstract: The Cohen structure theorem is an important tool in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry. Recent work of Caviglia, Goswami, and Mesiti addresses the related question of which unital rings admit a maximal ideal for which the natural projection admits a section; for such rings, they prove a structure theorem in terms of semidirect products of rings. In this paper, we extract the underlying mechanism of their structure theorem to address when unital rings admit a nonzero proper ideal whose associated projection map has this property. We also address other settings involving ideals with conditions which are determined by ring theoretic properties of the corresponding quotient.

papers.title: Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups.

papers.title: Analytic and Numerical Investigation of a Proposed Non-linear Extension of Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: In this paper, additional properties of a previously introduced non-linear extension of quantum mechanics are investigated. Analytically, we uncover a limit in which the model reduces to ordinary linear quantum mechanics. We also perform a perturbation analysis about an exact solution studied in earlier work. The equations represent a system that is subject to a periodic driver, and we use Floquet theory to help determine its properties. Numerically, we compare the exact solution to the analytic approximation, and we exhibit several examples of how the non-linear effects influence particle trajectories, with particular emphasis on trajectories near the linear limit.

papers.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in genera four and five, and of mixed Tate subquotients of $H_c^{2g}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ associated with shuffle algebras and multiple zeta values in every genus.

papers.title: The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121
papers.abstract: We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus. At $p = 17$ and $43$ one Hecke block of the Mordell-Weil group has logarithm divisible by $p^2$ but $p$-adic height of valuation one, and a comparison of valuations in the quadratic Chabauty identity then shows that each CM point is the only rational point in its residue disc, with no computation of the local height at $p$, no basis of the Mordell-Weil group and no equations for the curve. The inputs come from expansions of differentials at CM points and from a formula we prove for intersection numbers of CM divisors of coprime fundamental discriminants under Hecke operators on $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(\ell^e)$ (Theorem 1.3).

papers.title: Iterative constructions of semifields 2-dimensional over a nucleus
papers.abstract: The construction of finite semifields dates back to Dickson's work in 1906. To the best of our knowledge, only two iterative constructions were previously known: those of Hiramine, Matsumoto and Oyama in 1987, and of Kantor and Williams in 2004. The latter yields, for suitable even orders, superpolynomially many pairwise non-isotopic semifields. In this paper, we use skew-polynomial rings to give a new iterative construction of finite semifields. This construction produces large families of pairwise non-isotopic semifields, each of which is $2$-dimensional over one of its nuclei. In particular, we show that this construction method yields semifields not contained in any family of semifields known so far.

papers.title: On a critical nonlinear Schrödinger system with $K$-wise interaction: the cooperative case
papers.abstract: We study least energy fully non-trivial solutions of a nonlinear Schrödinger system with $K\ge3$ components and $K$-wise interaction, in the Sobolev critical regime. We consider bounded domains with Brezis--Nirenberg-type assumptions, and the associated homogeneous problem in $\mathbb R^N$. For every positive coupling, we prove the existence of a nonnegative ground state and identify a strictly positive threshold separating semi-trivial ground states from fully non-trivial ones. When the linear coefficients coincide, a finite-dimensional reduction gives an exact formula for the ground state energy and a characterization of all nonnegative ground states. In particular, above the threshold all ground states are synchronized; for sufficiently strong cooperation, their amplitude vector is unique and has an explicit asymptotic behavior. We also establish existence results for positive synchronized solutions beyond the ground state regime. For sufficiently weak cooperation, we obtain least energy positive solutions in the critical ternary case $N=K=3$, by minimizing on the component-wise Nehari set and ruling out critical concentration. The analysis includes the endpoint interaction exponent $q=1$, where the energy functional is not differentiable.

papers.title: An Explicit Three-Dimensional Dispersing Billiard with Finite Horizon
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit three-dimensional periodic Lorentz gas whose quotient by the period lattice \(2\Z^3\) has 38 spherical scatterers with rational centers and four rational radii. The scatterers are strictly separated, so the associated dispersing billiard has no corners or cusps. We prove finite horizon by establishing a common blocking margin for every rational direction. A projected-lattice estimate for the face-centered cubic core leaves nine exceptional directions, handled by a finite line-space covering certificate. Simultaneous rational approximation transfers this margin to every direction and yields an explicit upper horizon bound. All finite calculations use exact arithmetic, with verification data and algorithms included. The positive separation and blocking margins also ensure stability under sufficiently small independent perturbations of the centers and radii.

papers.title: Formally Verified Semidefinite Programming
papers.abstract: We present a formally verified Rust implementation of a first-order semidefinite programming solver, a nontrivial piece of numerical software. We wrote the solver by hand and then directed Claude to generate the entire verification in Verus, an automated theorem prover for Rust programs. We discuss the algorithm underlying the solver, its implementation in Rust, and our pragmatic approach to proving it correct in Verus.

papers.title: Convexity is overrated: Shortest paths on 4-polytopes are hard to compute
papers.abstract: We prove that computing geodesic distance on the boundary of a rational convex $4$-polytope is NP-hard. We then construct rational $4$-polytopes with two rational points joined by exponentially many shortest paths of equal rational length, disproving several conjectures along the way. For the same problem, we also prove SQRTSUM-hardness under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. By a separate argument, we show that the square of the geodesic distance between distinct rational boundary points of a rational convex polytope is a totally positive multiquadratic number.

papers.title: The low-degree sample complexity of clustering Gaussian mixtures with more groups than dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the computational limits of clustering $n$ observations drawn from a mixture of $K$ isotropic Gaussian distributions in $\mathbb R^d$, when the number $K$ of groups is much larger than the dimension $d$. In this regime, distance-based and spectral procedures require a squared separation $Δ^2$ of order $\sqrt d$. In contrast, tensor-based procedures cluster at a polylogarithmic separation but need a sample size that is a large polynomial of $dK$, and the low-degree lower bounds known for random centers only show that $n$ must exceed $dK^2$. Focusing on normally distributed centers, we characterize the minimal separation for clustering with low-degree polynomials in the regime $K>d$, through a low-degree lower bound and a matching upper bound, up to subpolynomial factors. In particular, for $K=d^{p/2}$ with $p> 2$ a real number, we show that a sample size of the order of $K^3 d^{(\lceil p\rceil-p)/2}$ is required to recover the clustering with subpolynomial separation, and that it suffices when $p$ is not an integer.

papers.title: On the ring of bounded functions on the character variety
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ denote the character variety associated to the group $(o_L, +)$, where $o_L$ is the ring of integers in a finite extension $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$. $\mathfrak{X}$ is a rigid analytic variety parametrizing locally $L$-analytic characters. Let $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)$ denote the global sections bounded by $1$. In this paper we prove that $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)= o_L[[o_L]]$, answering the question posed in [AB24].

papers.title: Small-Gain Analysis of Robust Event-Triggered Extremum Seeking for Scalar Maps
papers.abstract: We study a sample-and-hold implementation of gradient extremum seeking for a scalar quadratic map in which the control signal is refreshed only when an event occurs.
